newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian PM gears up to fight parliament.
newsitem.headline: Russian PM gears up to fight parliament.

text.p: Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, girding himself for a tough battle with both chambers of parliament, on Thursday cautioned government ministers to be ready for surprises ahead.
Russian news agencies quoted Chernomyrdin as telling a cabinet meeting that all ministers had to attend a session of the State Duma lower house of parliament on Friday to defend the 1997 budget.
"You must be ready for every possibility. Anything could happen," Itar-Tass quoted him as telling ministers.
The Duma, which is dominated by the opposition and which has rejected the cabinet's original draft budget, will discuss a compromise spending plan worked out by a conciliatory commission.
Chernomyrdin told ministers to defend the plan at the session, admitting that "the situation in the economy is very complicated, especially over payment of wages and pensions".
An unresolved conflict between the government and the Duma might lead to President Boris Yeltsin having to make a choice between dismissing either of the bodies.

Later on Thursday, Chernomyrdin faces another test when the Federation Council considers the situation over unpaid pensions and wages which has already forced thousands of miners across Russian to go on strike.

On Wednesday, the normally compliant Federation Council was in uncharacteristic uproar against the prime minister after Chernomyrdin, pleading illness, refused to appear to explain how he planned to solve the economic crisis.
Some Council members, who are drawn from Russia's regional leaders, called for a motion of no confidence in Chernomyrdin's government and questioned its ability to handle the situation.

The liberal governor of Nizhny Novgorod region, Boris Nemtsov, told Council speaker Yegor Stroyev during the debate: "You've got to go to Chernomyrdin and ask him if he has the will and the courage to work on in this post or not."
"If we don't take steps, then...the people will rise up and millions will take to the streets," warned Vladimir Shtygashev, parliamentary speaker of the Khakasia region in Siberia.
The government took the unusual step of issuing a statement, stressing its "readiness for constructive and permanent dialogue with the federal legislature in solving our toughest social problems."
It also expressed "astonishment" at the "irresponsible speculation" of deputies.

President Boris Yeltsin, 65, who underwent a multiple heart bypass operation on November 5, is due to meet Council speaker Stroyev on Thursday at his country residence where he moved on Wednesday from the nearby Barvikha sanatorium.
Chernomyrdin, speaking at the government session on Thursday, attacked the Federation Council as "strange", according to Interfax news agency.
"Why does it happen that the moment the situation in the economy starts to improve, a storm starts?," Chernomyrdin was quoted as saying.
